Net radiation at the land surface

Source: R/metric-radiation.R
ef_net_radiation.Rd

Computes the instantaneous net radiation \(R_n\) at the land surface, i.e. the radiant energy available at the surface for the soil, sensible and latent heat fluxes, as the balance between the absorbed incoming shortwave radiation, the incoming longwave radiation, the longwave radiation emitted by the surface and the part of the incoming longwave radiation that the surface reflects. This is the surface radiation balance used in the METRIC energy balance model.

Usage

ef_net_radiation(rs_in, albedo, rl_in, rl_out, emissivity)

Arguments

rs_in

Numeric. Incoming (downwelling) shortwave radiation at the surface, instantaneous at the satellite overpass time [W m-2]. Must be finite and >= 0.

albedo

Numeric. Broadband surface albedo [-]. Must lie in [0, 1].

rl_in

Numeric. Incoming (downwelling) longwave radiation at the surface [W m-2]. Must be finite and > 0.

rl_out

Numeric. Longwave radiation emitted by the surface [W m-2], i.e. \(\varepsilon_0 \sigma T_s^4\). It must not include the reflected incoming longwave component, which the function accounts for separately. Must be finite and > 0.

emissivity

Numeric. Broadband surface emissivity \(\varepsilon_0\) [-]. Must lie in (0, 1]. It must be the same emissivity used to compute rl_out; ensuring this consistency is the responsibility of the caller.

Value

A numeric vector of net radiation \(R_n\) [W m-2] with the common length of the inputs. If the inputs include matrices or arrays (all with the same dim), the result keeps that dim. Negative values are physically possible (e.g. at night or over snow) and are returned unchanged.

Details

The surface radiation balance is $$R_n = (1 - \alpha) R_{s\downarrow} + R_{L\downarrow} - R_{L\uparrow} - (1 - \varepsilon_0) R_{L\downarrow}$$ where \(\alpha\) is albedo, \(R_{s\downarrow}\) is rs_in, \(R_{L\downarrow}\) is rl_in, \(R_{L\uparrow}\) is rl_out and \(\varepsilon_0\) is emissivity. The last term is the incoming longwave radiation reflected by the surface.

Assumptions:

  • all fluxes are instantaneous and refer to the same time (the satellite overpass);

  • the balance is one-dimensional (per pixel or per point), with no lateral exchange;

  • emissivity is the emissivity used to obtain rl_out from the surface temperature.

If rl_out already contains the total upwelling longwave radiation (emitted plus reflected), for example from a radiometer measurement, the equivalent call is emissivity = 1, which removes the reflected term and avoids counting it twice.

Missing values (NA, NaN) in any input propagate to the corresponding output element, without errors or warnings. Diagnostic flags for missing inputs are assembled by the orchestration layer, not by this function.

Arguments must be numeric (double or integer) and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled. Values outside the domain (albedo outside [0, 1], emissivity outside (0, 1], negative rs_in, non-positive rl_in or rl_out, or any infinite value) raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error) that names the argument and the number of offending values. Invalid inputs are expected to be masked or flagged upstream by quality control; values are never silently corrected.

The form of the equation has been cross-checked against independent secondary sources; verification against the primary reference (Allen et al., 2007) is pending.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Examples

# Single pixel: rl_out = 0.98 * 5.67e-8 * 300^4 (surface at 300 K)
ef_net_radiation(
  rs_in = 800, albedo = 0.20, rl_in = 320,
  rl_out = 450.0846, emissivity = 0.98
)
#> [1] 503.5154

# Several pixels sharing one incoming longwave value (recycled)
ef_net_radiation(
  rs_in = c(750, 800, 820),
  albedo = c(0.15, 0.20, 0.25),
  rl_in = 320,
  rl_out = c(440, 450, 470),
  emissivity = c(0.97, 0.98, 0.96)
)
#> [1] 507.9 503.6 452.2

# rl_out given as total upwelling longwave (emitted + reflected)
ef_net_radiation(
  rs_in = 800, albedo = 0.20, rl_in = 320,
  rl_out = 456.4846, emissivity = 1
)
#> [1] 503.5154
